record.original_question: Determine the maximum number of circles of radius 1 that can be placed inside a circle of radius n so that no two overlap except possibly by tangency. More generally, study the analogous problem for variable radii i(n), for packing unit circles into a given triangle, and for analogous packing problems involving spheres, cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, and other planar or spatial figures.

evidence.quote: What is the maximum number of circles of radius 1, at most tangential by twos, which are included into a circle of radius n? ... Study a similar problem for circles of radius 1 included into a given triangle ... Similar questions for spheres, cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, etc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $f(n)$ denote the maximum number of closed unit disks (disks of radius $1$) that can be placed inside a closed disk of radius $n$ in the Euclidean plane such that no two of the unit disks have overlapping interiors (i.e., any two are either disjoint or tangent). 

(a) Determine $f(n)$ as a function of $n$, or give sharp upper and lower bounds.

(b) More generally, for a function $i(n) > 0$, determine the maximum number of disks of radius $i(n)$ that can be packed (interiors disjoint) into a disk of radius $n$.

(c) Solve the analogous packing problem for unit disks inside a given triangle in the plane.

(d) Investigate the analogous packing problems in three-dimensional Euclidean space for unit balls inside a ball, and for the packing of congruent cones, cylinders, regular pyramids, and other planar or spatial convex bodies into a prescribed region.
artifact.status_search_result: Packing congruent circles into a circle is a classical problem in discrete geometry. Optimal configurations are rigorously known only for a small number of values (n = 1–7, 10–14, 19), while many other cases have only conjectured optima. The general problem—including the analogous problems for triangles, balls, cones, cylinders, and pyramids—remains open, with no closed-form formula known.

status_evidence.claim: Only finitely many cases are rigorously solved; the general problem is open.

status_evidence.claim: Many configurations are only known via numerical/heuristic search, not proof.
